before.body:
## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Sharing interjections → AI social engagement.” Clarified intent: sharing is the primary feature; the social-media idea is that an AI can more easily turn a selected interjection and its source context into a draft post.

Additional product research distinguishes the immutable private capture from a separately reviewed share revision.

## Outcome

A user can deliberately package and share one or more interjections without exposing the whole local session. The user may optionally ask their ChatBot to generate a social-ready draft from the selected interjection, source attribution, and bounded anchor context.

The app shares an inspectable package or user-approved rendered representation. It does not publish directly to a social network by default.

## Product boundary

### Private capture

The local capture may retain raw audio, raw transcription, cleaned transcription, source anchors, and other private session evidence according to local retention policy.

### Reviewed share revision

The sender selects what will represent them:

- original raw recording
- a separate re-recording
- raw transcript
- edited or approved transcript
- text-only representation
- TTS generated from approved text
- omitted/private interjection

Selecting one representation must not silently upload the others. TTS and materially AI-edited wording require visible provenance and disclosure. The private capture remains unchanged when a share revision is created.

A “Preview as recipient” step should show the selected representation, source context, attribution, reveal suggestion, and every field or attachment that will leave the device.

## Repository fit

The current app already exports a selected interjection with source anchors and supports Markdown/JSON session handoff. This issue formalizes a smaller share boundary and optional drafting step rather than introducing a feed, account system, or social backend.

## Proposed share contract

Add a canonical `spoken-margins.interjection-package.v1` containing:

- package ID, schema version, creation time, and deterministic content digest
- one or more interjections with stable local IDs and package-scoped IDs
- source identity: canonical URL/reference, title, media type, publisher/author when known
- target and durable anchor evidence sufficient for later resolution
- selected user-approved representation and provenance
- optional audio attachment only when selected
- optional AI response or summary excerpts selected explicitly
- optional author display label; no hidden device/account identifiers
- rights/copyright warning metadata and source-material inclusion flags
- redaction record showing fields omitted before export
- optional parent package digest for later reply/fork lineage
- optional sender reveal-mode suggestion that never overrides recipient policy

The lossless package is JSON. Human-readable Markdown or plain text may accompany it.

Do not freeze a cross-edition acoustic shape until #27 reports which evidence is useful. The package must remain transport-neutral; ActivityPub research is tracked separately in #25.

## Privacy and consent UX

Before export, show exactly which fields leave the device:

- interjection text/transcript
- source reference and anchor excerpt
- audio, if selected
- AI-generated content, if selected
- author label, if entered
- synthetic-voice or AI-edit provenance
- source-material and rights warnings

Default to the minimum useful package. Never include API keys, diagnostics, full source text, unrelated turns, precise private filesystem paths, or unselected raw representations.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A selected interjection can be exported and re-imported byte-for-byte at the contract layer.
- [ ] Digest verification detects modification and produces a clear invalid-package state.
- [ ] Default export excludes audio, full source text, diagnostics, unrelated session data, and unselected representations.
- [ ] The preview accurately lists every included field and attachment.
- [ ] Raw, re-recorded, edited-text, text-only, and disclosed-TTS share revisions have fixtures.
- [ ] Draft fixtures cover short post, thread outline, long-form reflection, attribution, insufficient context, and copyrighted-excerpt limits.
- [ ] Share cancellation and destination failure leave the local session unchanged.
- [ ] Contract validation, export/import tests, privacy tests, AI prompt tests, and iOS build-for-testing pass.

## Non-goals

- No public timeline, follower graph, reactions, ranking, or engagement optimization.
- No direct social-network account integration in the first implementation.
- No remote mutable document.
- No claim that package authorship proves a legal identity.
- No requirement that typed interjections from #15 exist before voice/transcript sharing.

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Post-Recovery-MVP foundation.
- Rights and provenance policy comes from #14.
- Findings from #27 inform cross-edition machine evidence.
- Blocks #18 and #25.
- #15 should be representable later but does not block the initial package.
- Device signing in #22 remains optional and must not block ordinary unsigned sharing.

- source identity and source-resolution status
- retained sender anchor evidence

- local enable/mute/delete state

before.title: [Spike] Resolve shared podcast anchors across differing audio editions
before.body:
## Source

Product research on shared and co-op interjections, 2026-07-21. Two listeners may resolve the same podcast episode through audio files that differ because of dynamic ads, silence trimming, re-encoding, corrections, or provider-specific versions.

## Question

Can Spoken Margins reliably relocate a shared interjection or Listening Map node onto the recipient's copy of the same editorial audio without redistributing the complete source and without confidently attaching commentary to the wrong passage?

This spike evaluates cross-edition resolution. It does not add a production sharing surface.

## Challenge model

Keep the evidence layers distinct:

- **Episode identity:** feed URL, item GUID, canonical episode URL, title, publisher, publication date, duration, and optional exact-edition digest.
- **Human anchor:** transcript excerpt, nearby text, chapter or Listening Map node, and sender media time.
- **Machine anchor:** versioned acoustic evidence around the source position.
- **Resolution result:** recipient-local position plus evidence class, confidence, ambiguity, and retained original evidence.

A sender timestamp is a hint, not a portable position. Dynamic insertions and deletions require a monotonic, piecewise mapping between sender and recipient timelines rather than one global offset.

## Current repository foundation

The current app already stores text, transcript, media-time, and turn anchors; playback position; nearby source context; transcript timelines; source references; and playback rate. Those are necessary inputs but do not yet prove cross-edition equivalence.

The existing playback-position `AnchorConfidence` describes how a local position was obtained. Do not overload it with cross-edition resolution status.

## Current research

### Transcript and identity baseline

Compare canonical source identity, exact-edition digest, timestamp, transcript quote, before/after context, and Listening Map nodes before adding acoustic evidence. Distinctive transcript context may solve many cases and remains inspectable by a person.

### Chromaprint baseline

Chromaprint is designed for compact fingerprints of near-identical audio, duplicate detection, and long-stream monitoring. Its raw fingerprint output and chunk/overlap support make it a plausible first benchmark, but it explicitly trades precision and robustness for search performance.

References:

- https://github.com/acoustid/chromaprint
- https://github.com/acoustid/chromaprint/blob/master/src/cmd/fpcalc.cpp
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acoustid/chromaprint/master/LICENSE.md

Treat suitability for short speech windows and dynamic podcast editions as an empirical question. Review LGPL-related distribution obligations and the selected decoding/FFT dependencies before proposing iOS integration.

### Multi-evidence resolution

Evaluate separate acoustic windows before and after each anchor, plus distributed Listening Map nodes. Several verified nodes may act as an alignment spine that identifies where timeline offsets change. Require local evidence to agree with global episode order.

Compare at least:

1. timestamp and duration only
2. transcript quote/context matching
3. acoustic matching
4. fused transcript, acoustic, identity, and map evidence

## Resolution evidence classes

The spike should recommend a transport-neutral result vocabulary such as:

- exact edition
- acoustically verified
- transcript verified
- map interpolated
- ambiguous
- absent from recipient edition
- unresolved

Only evidence classes justified by the benchmark should be eligible for automatic inline cues. Preserve sender evidence even after a recipient-local position is resolved.

## Risks

- false confident placement beside the wrong argument
- repeated theme music, jingles, ads, or silence producing ambiguous matches
- publisher edits, time stretching, pitch changes, or replaced passages
- codec delay, resampling, window-boundary, and algorithm-version drift
- inability to decode protected or provider-owned playback
- CPU, battery, storage, and latency costs on representative devices
- licensing and App Store distribution obligations
- copyright and privacy questions for shared fingerprints and transcript excerpts
- a recipient possessing a genuinely absent edition-specific segment

## Spike outputs

- a benchmark corpus of paired episode editions with ground-truth alignment
- comparison results for all four resolution approaches
- measured placement error, false-placement rate, unresolved rate, ambiguity rate, runtime, and storage
- an omission check covering speech-only passages, dynamic pre/mid/post-roll ads, repeated material, silence edits, re-encoding, and publisher corrections
- recommended anchor evidence and resolution-result contracts
- licensing and platform feasibility note
- explicit go/no-go recommendation for Chromaprint and for automatic placement

## Decision rule

A resolver that declines difficult anchors may be acceptable. A resolver that confidently places a friend's reaction beside the wrong passage is not.

Do not advance to production until the benchmark defines an automatic-placement threshold, a runner-up/ambiguity policy, and a human-review fallback. The spike must report failures and unresolved cases rather than optimizing only average accuracy.

## Dependencies and sequencing

- Blocked by the stable minimum portable-package and durable-anchor boundary in #17.
- Findings may define a versioned optional machine-evidence extension without destabilizing the base package contract.
- Blocks full cross-edition podcast acceptance in #18; exact-edition and context-only import experiments may proceed independently.
- #21 may later supply approximate microphone-derived evidence; it does not block this spike.
- Do not add this to the active Recovery MVP.

before.title: [Audit] Reconcile claimed interjection-sharing implementation with source
before.body:
## Problem

Comments added on 2026-08-22 to #17, #18, and #19 describe interjection sharing as implemented behind a gate, including a `.spokenmargins` package, `sharingExperienceEnabled`, imported layers, `conversationId`, and `docs/interjection-sharing-and-article-acquisition.md`.

A repository/default-branch audit on 2026-08-24 could not find those symbols, that document, the claimed imported-layer runtime, or a related branch. Until the implementation is located and reproduced, downstream classroom or asynchronous-conversation planning must treat those comments as unverified implementation claims rather than available infrastructure.

## Outcome

Resolve the discrepancy with one evidence-backed result:

1. locate the exact commit, branch, pull request, or recoverable artifact containing the implementation and reconcile it into the repository; or
2. correct the issue comments/status to say the work is design-approved or planned, not implemented.

## Evidence required if implementation exists

- canonical commit SHA and branch/PR ancestry;
- complete file inventory including the referenced design document;
- schema/version definitions for exported packages and imported layers;
- gate definition, default state, and route for enabling it;
- automated test/build evidence at that SHA;
- migration, privacy, tamper, and malformed-package behavior;
- explicit distinction between implemented, verified, and product-owner human-validated state.

## Required reconciliation if implementation does not exist

- Amend #17, #18, and #19 so their comments do not assert unavailable runtime behavior.
- Preserve useful design decisions as proposed contracts rather than deleting history.
- Make #17 the first implementation dependency for any package-based classroom pilot.
- Remove or repair any documentation, plan, or issue dependency that assumes imported layers already ship.

## Audit checklist

- [ ] Search all local and remote refs, pull requests, tags, stashes/artifacts available to the owner, and repository history for the claimed symbols and file.
- [ ] Confirm whether any located commit descends from or can apply cleanly to the current default branch.
- [ ] Run the contract validators, focused SessionKit tests, and relevant app build at the located/reconciled source.
- [ ] Exercise export/import with valid, malformed, unsupported-version, wrong-source, duplicate, and tampered fixtures.
- [ ] Record what is implemented, what is merely verified by automation, and what still requires product-owner validation.
- [ ] Update downstream dependencies in #70 and #82 to match the result.

## Audit and stopping rule

Search results or prose comments are not implementation evidence. Stop treating the sharing layer as implemented unless a buildable source revision, schema fixtures, and reproducible tests can be identified. If no artifact is found after all owner-accessible refs and histories are checked, close this audit by correcting the claims and reopening implementation planning under #17–#19.

## Non-goals

- Reimplementing sharing inside the audit issue.
- Publishing a server protocol or classroom backend.
- Calling the flow human-validated based on automated checks.

Related: #17, #18, #19, and #70.

before.body:
## Source

Handwritten product note, 2026-07-21: “Co-op interjections: layered asynchronous conversation.”

## Outcome

Two or more people can exchange immutable commentary layers around the same source, reply to specific interjections, and listen through the resulting conversation without creating a single mutable shared transcript or requiring simultaneous playback.

## Product principle

The source remains the common spine. Each participant owns a separate layer. Replies create lineage; they do not rewrite the parent package. The receiving user decides which layers are enabled and how they influence or interrupt playback.

This collaboration model is transport-neutral. Files/share sheet should be sufficient to validate it; a cloud relay or ActivityPub adapter may deliver the same immutable packages later.

## Proposed contract additions

Extend the package/import work from #17 and #18 with:

- `conversationId` scoped to a package lineage, not a global account
- `parentPackageDigest`
- `replyToInterjectionId` or `replyToPackageScopedId`
- participant display label and optional signer key ID
- monotonic package creation time plus local receipt time
- explicit fork/merge metadata when one package replies to several prior packages
- deterministic ordering rules that do not depend on server arrival order

Imported content remains immutable. Local mute, hide, and playback policy are separate state.

## Playback and UI behavior

- Present layers as a stack with participant labels, verification state, and reply lineage.
- Let users listen chronologically by source anchor or follow a reply thread.
- Preserve each recipient's Fresh, Companion, or Guided reveal policy from #18.
- Provide explicit modes for pause-and-play commentary, commentary-only review, and source-with-selected-layers.
- Always make it clear whether audio is the source, another participant, or an AI-generated turn.
- Return to the exact source position after commentary; never cascade into duplicate resumes.

## Exchange model

Start with package exchange through Files/share sheet. Define a transport boundary so a later encrypted link, CloudKit/service relay, or ActivityPub adapter can deliver the same immutable packages. Do not make remote sync or federation a prerequisite for validating the conversation model.

## Future attributed synthesis

AI editorial synthesis is tracked separately in #26. It must cite contributing margins, preserve disagreement and uncertainty, and require explicit user action. It is not part of the minimum co-op conversation.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A participant can reply to a specific imported interjection and export a child package without altering the parent.
- [ ] A recipient can import parent and child packages in either order and reconstruct the same lineage.
- [ ] Duplicate, missing-parent, forked, conflicting-label, and invalid-signature states are explicit and tested.
- [ ] Source-order and thread-order playback are deterministic.
- [ ] Muting or deleting one local layer never mutates or deletes another layer or local interjection.
- [ ] Backgrounding, route changes, and lock-screen transport preserve source ownership and resume position.
- [ ] Package fixtures, persistence migrations, SessionKit tests, UI tests, and iOS build-for-testing pass.
- [ ] Product-owner validation shows at least one conversation continuing beyond the initial one-way exchange.

## Non-goals

- No engagement feed, likes, follower graph, read receipts, typing indicators, or presence status.
- No collaborative editing of another person's words.
- No AI-generated reply inserted without a clear actor label and explicit user action.
- No dependency on ActivityPub research in #25.
- No AI synthesis dependency for the basic conversation.

## Dependencies and stopping rule

Blocked by #17 and #18. Do not implement before the Recovery MVP is human-validated and one-way imported commentary has passed bounded device checks. Blocks the attributed synthesis work in #26.

before.title: [Post-MVP] Classroom assignments, interjection returns, and app-observed participation receipts
before.body:
## Outcome

Add a **Classroom** experience in which one or more teachers can distribute a source assignment to one or more students. Students may listen in Spoken Margins, read through an instrumented Spoken Margins reading surface, or use a clearly labeled external/self-attested route; they can interject while working and return a reviewable packet containing their selected interjections and source anchors.

An optional higher-trust mode can also return an **app-observed participation receipt** derived from #80: a conservative account of supported playback, in-app presentation, and interjection events, with policy-selected user-presence authorization at each interjection. This is evidence about app-observed presentation and payload integrity—not proof of attention, comprehension, legal identity, authorship, or academic honesty.

## Actors and ownership

- **Teacher:** creates and distributes an assignment, chooses recipients and evidence policy, and reviews returned packets.
- **Co-teacher:** may administer or review the same assignment according to explicit permissions.
- **Student:** accepts the assignment, controls what personal material is returned within the declared assignment policy, and can inspect the packet before submission.
- **Class/group:** owns membership and assignment access rules; membership must not silently expose one student's work to another.
- **Spoken Margins client:** records source-relative playback and interjection events it can actually observe.
- **Transport/service:** distributes immutable assignment revisions and returns submissions idempotently; it must not become the authority for claims the client did not observe.

## Core workflow

1. A teacher creates an assignment with a stable ID, item/source identity and edition, instructions, due date, recipients/groups, allowed interjection representations, and requested participation-evidence policy.
2. The assignment is distributed to selected students. Updates create explicit revisions rather than silently changing work already in progress.
3. A student accepts or declines the assignment, acquires the source through a lawful supported path, and chooses to listen in Spoken Margins, read through its instrumented reading surface, or declare an external/self-attested route. The selected mode must not change the source/edition binding.
4. The student makes anchored interjections during the item. Classroom policy may require fresh user-presence authorization for each submitted interjection.
5. Before submission, the student previews every field and attachment that will leave the device.
6. The app returns an immutable, digest-addressed packet containing the assignment revision, selected interjections, source anchors, and optional participation receipt.
7. Teachers can verify integrity, inspect gaps and unsupported intervals, review interjections in source order, and export or provide feedback without mutating the student's original packet.

## Typed data boundaries

Keep these layers distinct:

### Assignment

- assignment ID, revision, class ID, issuer(s), recipients/groups
- item/source identity, exact edition when known, and acquisition/reference instructions
- teacher prompt, due date, reveal/playback policy, and required return fields
- requested authentication and participation-evidence policy
- rights, privacy, retention, and late/resubmission policy

### Student work

- submission ID and revision/attempt lineage
- selected interjection representations and provenance
- durable source anchors and relevant bounded context
- student-visible edits, redactions, or omissions
- optional replies/feedback lineage
- no unrelated sessions, diagnostics, raw media, or private drafts by default

### Participation evidence

- versioned source-relative listening and in-app reading observations supplied by #80
- listening boundaries including seek/pause/rate changes, replay, interruptions, and declared offline gaps
- conservative in-app reading presentation intervals; open, navigation, or rapid scroll alone does not establish coverage
- explicit external/self-attested and unobserved states rather than fabricated reading telemetry
- interjection capture time plus source position/anchor
- assignment/source/revision binding, per-mode canonical intervals, and deterministic union coverage
- event or packet digests, signing metadata, and verifier result
- explicit states for observed, self-attested, unavailable, interrupted, unsigned, invalid, and unsupported evidence

### Identity and authorization

- class/account membership is separate from device-key continuity
- biometric/passcode authorization may show that an enrolled device credential authorized a specific frozen event or payload
- the design must not equate one device key with one student or claim that biometrics establish legal identity
- account recovery, shared devices, device replacement, key rotation, accessibility-compatible fallback, and teacher policy exceptions must be explicit

## Trust model and limits

The receipt can make tampering and silent bulk submission harder and can show that a supported client recorded a sequence of source-presentation/interjection events under a declared algorithm. Reading evidence means only that an in-app surface presented bounded source ranges; it is not eye tracking. The receipt cannot prove that the student:

- paid attention to the source
- understood the material
- was the only person near or using the device
- did not use another player or source
- did not receive outside help
- is globally unique or legally identified

Teacher-facing language should say **verified packet integrity**, **device-authorized interjection**, and **app-observed listening activity** where supported. Avoid “proof of learning,” “proof of presence,” or unqualified “proof of work.”

## Privacy, minors, and accessibility

- Collect the minimum evidence needed for the teacher's declared policy.
- Show the policy before a student accepts the assignment and show a complete submission preview.
- Do not record ambient audio, camera data, background activity, precise location, or unrelated app/device activity as listening evidence.
- Define retention, deletion, withdrawal, guardian/school consent, educator access, audit access, and export rules before any hosted classroom pilot.
- Treat applicable student-record, child-privacy, school-procurement, accessibility, and source-rights requirements as launch gates requiring policy/legal review rather than assumptions in the client.
- Provide a meaningful accessible fallback when biometric authorization is unavailable or inappropriate; never mislabel fallback evidence as biometric.
- A student must be able to distinguish required assignment evidence from optional product analytics.

## Proposed delivery sequence

### Phase 1 — transport-neutral classroom packets

Implement #82 by extending the verified portable-package boundary from #17 with assignment, source binding, recipient, submission, and attempt lineage. Validate link-based source acquisition and explicit return through Files/share sheet before building a classroom backend. Do not assume #17 is implemented until #81 resolves the current source/evidence discrepancy.

### Phase 2 — roles and delivery service

Add explicit class membership, co-teacher/student roles, invitations, assignment delivery, idempotent submission, revocation, and audit events behind transport-neutral domain protocols.

### Phase 3 — participation receipts

Build on the conservative observation ledger in #80 and the signing spike in #22. Compare an unsigned/minimized receipt, packet-only signing, per-interjection authorization, and append-only signed journey events. Select the least intrusive mechanism that meets the declared classroom policy; a digest or device signature alone must not be presented as student identity.

## Acceptance evidence

- [ ] A class with two teachers and multiple students can distribute one immutable assignment revision to selected recipients without exposing membership or submissions outside authorized roles.
- [ ] A student can accept the assignment, listen or read through a supported evidence mode, create multiple anchored interjections, preview the outbound data, and submit a packet without mutating the local session.
- [ ] Teachers receive the same result after offline retry or duplicate delivery; submission is idempotent and attempt lineage is preserved.
- [ ] The return packet binds assignment revision, source/edition, interjections, anchors, selected representations, and optional participation receipt to a deterministic digest.
- [ ] Tampering with a returned field or signed event is detected; missing, invalid, unsupported, and partially observed evidence is shown rather than filled in or inferred as fact.
- [ ] Fixtures cover seeking, replay, playback-rate changes, pause/resume, interruptions, backgrounding, offline gaps, bounded in-app reading dwell, rapid scrolling, external/self-attested reading, mixed modes, source changes, late submission, resubmission, and assignment revision during work.
- [ ] Fresh authorization, cancellation, lockout, fallback, changed enrollment, device replacement, and shared-device paths are tested when per-interjection authorization is required.
- [ ] Automated tests prove that one student cannot read another student's submission and that a removed teacher cannot access later packets.
- [ ] Export and diagnostics exclude private keys, unrelated sessions, unselected raw representations, and undeclared analytics.
- [ ] Teacher UI consistently separates packet integrity, device authorization, app-observed activity, inference, and unknowns.
- [ ] Contract validation, persistence migration tests, SessionKit tests, privacy/authorization tests, and relevant iOS/Watch builds pass.
- [ ] The product owner human-validates the declared teacher and student flows after automated evidence is complete.

## Non-goals

- Grading interjections automatically.
- Proving comprehension, attention, authorship, legal identity, or absence of outside help.
- Surveillance outside the supported listening session.
- Requiring a public social graph, engagement feed, or student leaderboard.
- Building a full learning-management system in the first increment.
- Treating uninterrupted playback alone as evidence of learning.
- Requiring biometrics for ordinary non-Classroom interjections or exports.

## Dependencies and sequencing

- #81 must reconcile whether the #17–#19 sharing layer actually exists in source.
- #82 validates assignment/return value before accounts or a hosted classroom service.
- #17 owns reviewed portable interjection packages; #18 owns imported participant layers.
- #80 owns listening/in-app-reading observation semantics and optional receipts.
- #22 owns device-key signing and the limits of biometric user-presence authorization.
- #14 owns source excerpts, attribution, sharing, and retention policy; #27 owns cross-edition anchor behavior.
- #19 may later support teacher feedback and layered classroom discussion; #26 may synthesize cross-participant patterns. Neither should block one-way assignment and return.

This is post-MVP. Begin with contracts, threat modeling, fixtures, and a fake transport. Do not build hosted classroom accounts or market trusted participation until the receipt semantics, privacy policy, authorization boundaries, and product-owner workflow validation are satisfactory.

## Decision and stopping rule

Compare at least three alternatives before selecting the trust mechanism: (1) ordinary reviewed return packets, (2) one authorization at final submission, and (3) fresh authorization at each interjection with an append-only listening receipt. Evaluate student friction, accessibility, privacy, battery/storage cost, offline reliability, cheating resistance actually achieved, and teacher usefulness.

Stop or narrow the participation-receipt feature if teachers cannot interpret its limits correctly, students work around it in ways that make the receipt misleading, per-interjection authorization materially disrupts listening, or the required data collection cannot meet the applicable privacy and school-policy bar.

## Actors and authority

- **Instructor/creator:** authors an assignment and one or more return destinations; may name co-instructors for display/review but package exchange alone does not grant server authority.
- **Participant/student:** imports the assignment, resolves the source, listens or reads, records interjections, reviews what will be returned, and explicitly exports it.
- **Reviewer:** imports returned packets and views each participant layer against the bound source.
- **Transport:** Files, share sheet, AirDrop, mail, learning-management upload, or another user-chosen carrier; transport is not identity, authorization, or durable delivery confirmation.

## Package boundaries

### Assignment package

- stable assignment ID, schema version, title, instructions, due date when supplied, and instructor display metadata;
- canonical public/source URL plus source identity/revision/digest expectations;
- acquisition guidance that routes through existing import flows;
- requested evidence policy, clearly distinguishing optional interjections from app-observed or self-attested participation;
- return destination hints without embedded credentials or executable routes.

The package must not redistribute copyrighted source content by default. Bundled content is permitted only when the exporting user has rights and the package contract explicitly supports it.

### Local work binding

- importing an assignment creates a durable binding between the assignment and a locally acquired item/source revision;
- assignment state must not overload or mutate the canonical `Session` playback model;
- mismatched, redirected, changed-edition, unavailable, or paywalled sources remain visible and recoverable rather than silently binding to the wrong item;
- ordinary unassigned library use remains unchanged.

- assignment and source binding;
- participant-chosen display identity appropriate to a package-only pilot;
- selected interjections with durable source anchors and required media assets;
- optional participation receipt from #80;
- package/schema versions, creation time, and integrity digest;
- no unrelated library history, raw event ledger, or unselected private interjections.

- Import multiple participant packets without overwriting the instructor's own layer or another participant.
- Show source mismatch, unsupported version, missing media, duplicate packet, and integrity warnings before import.
- Provide per-participant and source-position views, with explicit observed/self-attested/unobserved evidence labels.

before.title: [Post-MVP] Define portable Listening Map scenes and Skim summaries
before.body:
## Outcome

Define a versioned portable Listening Map contract that can carry ordered **scenes** and concise, source-grounded scene summaries for Skim without treating recipient-local timestamps as portable truth.

A scene is the product's neutral semantic navigation unit. It may represent a claim, topic, narrative scene, procedural step, or conversational movement; the user should not need to classify which.

This issue owns the contract, schema evolution, validators, fixtures, compatibility, and transport boundary. It does not own scene generation or playback controls.

## Product behavior enabled

A valid scene map can support:

- **Skim Forward:** summarize the current scene, then begin the next scene.
- **Skim Backward:** summarize the previous scene, then begin the current scene.
- exact-edition transport of scene structure and summaries;
- later cross-edition resolution without rewriting portable evidence;
- text-backed, transcript-backed, publisher-chapter, and prepared-audio representations;
- excluded or unresolved source intervals that remain playable but are not summarized.

The summary is a derivative bridge, not source quotation, not a transcript replacement, and not another scene.

## Challenge model

Keep these typed layers distinct.

### Source identity

- stable item/source identity;
- edition or revision identity when known;
- canonical source attribution;
- optional exact-edition digest;
- source type and language.

### Portable scene semantics

- stable scene ID and ordering;
- concise scene summary;
- optional navigation title;
- summary provenance and generation/version metadata;
- summary eligibility state and reason;
- source evidence sufficient to audit what the scene and summary cover.

The contract must not require a cinematic or rhetorical subtype. “Scene” is the user-facing abstraction.

### Durable anchor evidence

- source locator or text range for text-backed items;
- transcript segment/span and surrounding human-inspectable context for transcript-backed media;
- publisher chapter evidence when used;
- sender/source media time only as a hint;
- no local chunk index, UI position, or model-provided percentage as the sole anchor.

### Recipient-local resolution

Keep resolved start/end positions, evidence class, confidence, ambiguity, resolver version, and unresolved/absent outcomes separate from the portable scene. Do not overload the existing local-playback `AnchorConfidence` vocabulary.

An exact-edition scene may resolve directly. Automatic cross-edition placement remains governed by #27; ambiguous or absent scenes must remain unresolved rather than attaching to a plausible passage.

### Rights and disclosure

- source attribution accompanies transported scene summaries;
- full generated native-audio transcripts and large source excerpts remain excluded;
- generated summaries retain clear AI/derivative provenance;
- transport and preview follow the policy produced by #14;
- if scene maps are embedded in a `.spokenmargins` package, they follow #17's deterministic package and recipient-preview conventions.

## Ads and other non-scene audio

The contract must support audio that exists in the playable track but is absent from the scene structure.

Do not require user-visible ad labels. Internally, a span that is excluded or not positively eligible for summarization may remain playable and locally anchorable without receiving a scene summary. Absence of ad evidence must not imply summary eligibility.

## Compatibility and versioning

- Preserve `listening-map.v1` decoding and behavior.
- Do not silently reinterpret v1 chapters as fully grounded v2 scenes.
- Define explicit upgrade/import behavior and failure diagnostics.
- Update schema, runtime models, validators, fixtures, exports, and tests in one intentional change.
- Existing publisher chapters remain authoritative source structure and are never silently replaced.
- Mapless playback remains valid when no scene contract can be resolved.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A versioned schema represents ordered scenes, concise summaries, eligibility, provenance, durable anchor evidence, and recipient-local resolution without mixing those layers.
- [ ] v1 maps continue to validate and play with unchanged semantics.
- [ ] A v2 map round-trips deterministically and rejects invalid structure according to the repository's compatibility policy.
- [ ] Fixtures cover native text, prepared text audio, an exact-edition podcast, publisher chapters, dynamically inserted unlabeled audio, excluded/unknown spans, an unresolved cross-edition scene, and an absent scene.
- [ ] Every valid scene resolves monotonically to source evidence on its producing edition.
- [ ] A transported summary remains traceable to its scene and source evidence without transporting a full native-audio transcript.
- [ ] Summary provenance distinguishes source text, publisher-supplied text, deterministic transformation, and model-generated derivatives.
- [ ] Invalid scene structure or unresolved anchors never destroy the prior valid map or block mapless playback.
- [ ] Exports and diagnostics have negative tests proving that internal transcripts, large excerpts, and private paths do not leak.
- [ ] Contract validators, focused SessionKit tests, migration tests, and relevant app builds pass.
- [ ] Product-owner validation remains distinct from automated verification.

## Audit and falsification

Compare:

1. current `listening-map.v1`;
2. a minimal scene extension that stores local timestamps;
3. the selected portable-evidence plus local-resolution design.

Use omission checks for attribution, negation, speaker identity, summary provenance, excluded audio, exact-edition identity, unresolved cross-edition placement, publisher chapters, and v1 compatibility.

Treat any of the following as a stopping failure:

- a local timestamp is presented as a portable cross-edition position;
- ambiguous evidence is automatically placed;
- a scene summary cannot be traced to its covered source;
- excluded/unknown audio is implicitly eligible for summarization;
- full generated native-audio transcript text leaks through a map or package;
- v1 maps change meaning after the migration.

## Dependencies and related work

- #14 owns rights, attribution, excerpt, AI-derived-material, and sharing policy.
- #17 owns deterministic `.spokenmargins` packaging and recipient preview when this map is shared inside that transport.
- #27 owns cross-edition podcast-anchor benchmarking and automatic-placement thresholds.
- #46 supplies publisher podcast chapters and mapless fallback.
- #51 owns server-hosted native-audio Listening Map feasibility and exact source-position requirements.
- #48 is advanced cross-item semantic research and is not required for scene maps.
- #80 owns source-coverage accounting; summaries and skipped source must remain distinct there.

## Non-goals

- No scene generation pipeline.
- No Skim controls or playback bridge state.
- No public transcript reader.
- No public content index or cross-item semantic graph.
- No claim that semantic compression alone establishes a right to redistribute.
- No authorization to enter an active release lane; implementation requires a later product-owner release-plan update.

## Outcome

Add **Skim Forward** and **Skim Backward** as semantic playback controls alongside the existing independently configurable time-skip controls.

- **Skim Forward:** speak a concise summary of the current scene, then begin the next scene.
- **Skim Backward:** speak a concise summary of the previous scene, then begin the current scene.

A scene is the product's neutral semantic navigation unit from #88. It may represent a claim, topic, narrative scene, procedural step, or conversational movement.

This issue owns player state, navigation semantics, UI and accessibility, compact-surface capability publication, bridge playback, cancellation/repetition behavior, and verification. It does not own scene generation or the portable map schema.

## Why Skim and time skip coexist

Time skip and Skim solve different jobs:

- **Time skip** provides literal, fine-grained movement by a user-configurable duration.
- **Skim** provides semantic movement across a scene boundary with compressed context.

Do not automatically replace, retune, or hide time-skip settings when Skim becomes available. A listener may choose shorter time jumps once scene navigation exists, but that remains the listener's decision.

If a listener is 90% through a scene and presses Skim Forward, the bridge summarizes the **whole current scene**. If they only want to move through the remaining seconds, they can use their configured time-skip control.

## Canonical interaction

For previous scene `S-1`, current scene `S0`, and next scene `S+1`:

```text
Skim Backward:  summary(S-1) -> start(S0)
Skim Forward:   summary(S0)  -> start(S+1)
```

Beginning the current scene after a backward skim is intentional. Resuming at the original halfway position would act like “remind me” rather than semantic backward navigation and could return mid-thought immediately after a context summary.

The generated summary is a temporary bridge. It is not a source quotation, not another scene, and cannot recursively participate in Skim.

## Typed playback state

Keep these layers distinct:

### Canonical source state

- active item/target;
- accepted source or media position;
- duration;
- current resolved scene;
- playback rate;
- active source representation and readiness.

### Skim command state

- direction;
- origin position and origin scene;
- summary scene;
- destination scene and resolved landing;
- command sequence/repetition identity;
- unavailable/fallback reason.

### Bridge state

- generated summary text/audio identity and provenance;
- playing, paused, cancelled, failed, or completed state;
- progress within the bridge;
- retained source origin and destination;
- optional interjection target/provenance if the listener interjects during the bridge.

Bridge duration is not added to canonical source duration or source media time.

### Landing state

After a completed bridge, perform one accepted transition to the resolved scene boundary and resume through the ordinary source player. Do not maintain a second hidden position that can drift from Now Playing, persisted session state, interjection anchoring, or the scrubber.

## Control behavior during a bridge

The listener retains control throughout:

- pause/resume pauses or resumes the bridge;
- direct seeking or a configured time skip cancels the bridge under an explicit deterministic rule and moves through ordinary source transport;
- repeated same-direction Skim traverses additional scenes rather than replaying the same bridge;
- opposite-direction Skim cancels/reverses under an explicit tested rule;
- back/cancel provides a recoverable path to the saved origin;

## Boundaries and unavailable states

- At the first scene, Skim Backward restarts or remains at the first scene without fabricating previous context.
- At the final scene, Skim Forward summarizes it and reaches the item's normal end behavior.
- A repeated backward command after landing must step farther backward rather than trapping the listener in the same previous-summary/current-start pair.
- Excluded or unknown spans from #88/#89 receive no bridge. Commands within them navigate predictably to neighboring valid scene boundaries without exposing a convenient user-visible ad label.
- If no valid scene map or summary is available, Skim is unavailable with an honest capability state; it must not silently degrade into a time skip.
- A malformed/unresolved destination leaves source playback at a recoverable accepted position and reports the failure.
- Publisher chapter navigation and ordinary mapless playback remain available independently.

## UI and accessibility

On the full playback surface, semantic and time transport must be distinguishable without relying only on icon shape or position.

Candidate accessible names:

- “Skim backward one scene”
- “Back 15 seconds” using the configured value
- “Forward 30 seconds” using the configured value
- “Skim forward one scene”

The exact visual arrangement requires product-owner validation and must work with Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, increased contrast, Reduce Motion, and one-handed use.

Compact surfaces may expose Skim only when their command vocabulary and active runtime capability can represent it honestly. Do not silently repurpose standard Lock Screen, headphone, car, or Watch time-skip commands as Skim. Any user-configurable remapping must be explicit and reversible.

If new command IDs, snapshot fields, or capability values are required, update schemas, validators, runtime, fixtures, traces, and tests together.

## Coverage and provenance

Align with #80:

- source audio actually played remains observed source presentation;
- source skipped by Skim remains skipped/unobserved;
- hearing a generated bridge does not count as hearing the underlying source scene;
- replay caused by Skim Backward may count only the source audio actually presented after landing;
- bridge playback retains AI/derivative provenance and is never labeled as source speech.

Diagnostics must record IDs, states, positions, evidence classes, and timing without logging private full transcripts or unrelated interjection content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Skim Forward from any point in an eligible scene speaks that scene's whole summary and begins the next scene.
- [ ] Skim Backward from any point in an eligible scene speaks the previous scene's summary and begins the current scene.
- [ ] Separately configurable forward/back time skips remain available and unchanged.
- [ ] A 90%-complete scene still receives its whole-scene Skim summary; time skip remains the precise alternative.
- [ ] Pause, resume, cancel, time seek, same-direction repetition, opposite-direction reversal, interruption, backgrounding, and relaunch have deterministic state-machine coverage.
- [ ] Repeated Skim Backward commands move progressively backward and never loop on one scene pair.
- [ ] Bridge playback never changes canonical source duration, falsely advances source coverage, or shifts an interjection/source anchor.
- [ ] The source player, scrubber, persisted session, Now Playing state, and landing anchor agree after every completed or cancelled Skim.
- [ ] Excluded/unknown spans receive no summary and do not appear as convenient labeled ad nodes.
- [ ] Missing, malformed, ambiguous, or unresolved scene data produces an honest unavailable/recoverable state rather than a time-skip fallback.
- [ ] A listener can undo an accidental Skim and recover the saved origin.
- [ ] VoiceOver distinguishes Skim from configured time skips and announces the direction and scene-level effect.
- [ ] Capability-constrained surfaces never advertise Skim when they can only perform ordinary time transport.
- [ ] Contract validators, focused SessionKit tests, app-model tests, UI accessibility tests, interruption/restoration tests, and proportional builds pass.
- [ ] Automated evidence may mark the feature `verified`; only product-owner use may mark it `human_validated`.

Compare four alternatives on the same listening corpus:

1. configurable time skips only;
2. chapter jumps with no bridge;
3. Skim Forward only;
4. symmetric Skim Forward/Backward plus time skips.

- immediate undo/reversal rate;
- comprehension of the skipped/current context;
- whether listeners predict the landing correctly;
- bridge start latency;
- control-response latency;
- summary/source confusion;
- unwanted repetition;
- accessibility comprehension.

- backward resuming at the old halfway point;
- repeated back becoming stuck;
- a bridge being counted as source coverage;
- bridge duration shifting the scrubber;
- an interjection during a bridge anchoring to the future landing point;

- No authorization to enter an active release lane; implementation requires a later product-owner release-plan update.

- whether the item can still be played through a fallback.

## Goal

This issue intentionally owns the Library-screen portion of that audit; Item Detail and Margins are tracked separately.

## Requested changes

### Reduce the massive header / wasted vertical space

The current Library composition spends too much vertical space on header/chrome before the user reaches library content. Tighten the top hierarchy without shrinking important tap targets or making the screen visually cramped.

### Move Offline Rendering higher

Move **Offline Rendering** near the top of the Library, immediately after the primary header area, so preparation state/action is discoverable without scrolling through less actionable content first.

This is presentation only; preparation policy and correctness remain owned by #64/#73/#98.

### Default-hide items without a completed session

The product-owner audit requests that Library default to hiding items that do not have a completed session.

Implement this as a reversible presentation/filter rule, not deletion:

- hidden items remain available through an explicit scope/filter;
- completion must use the canonical item/session semantics from #102 rather than arbitrary historical sessions or AI-turn completion;
- changing the filter must not alter completion state.

Validate the exact product behavior with the realistic library before closure because this filter materially changes what appears by default.

### Sort by number of margins

Add a Library sort option for **number of margins**, enabling items with more user engagement to be surfaced together.

- define deterministic tie-breaking;
- derive the count from canonical margins/interjections rather than transient UI state;
- sorting must remain performant on a realistically large library and should be included in #93 profiling if necessary.

### Move session export out of Library

Remove **Export Sessions** from Library once the replacement Margins workflow is available. Export is an action on accumulated engagement, so its destination is tracked in the Margins workspace issue rather than duplicated here.

### Compact Library Now Playing

The Library's Now Playing treatment is currently approximately 1.5 inches tall and mostly empty space. Make it compact:

- remove the low-value/redundant icon called out in the audit;
- retain only the information/actions required to identify and return to active playback;
- avoid reproducing the full playback card inside Library.

before.title: UI regression: swipe navigation transition does not track the gesture interactively
before.body:
## Summary

Horizontal swipe navigation in the current UI feels delayed: the user swipes, then the destination navigates after the gesture rather than moving continuously with the finger.

The product-owner audit describes the desired behavior as effectively **navigate as I swipe**, not **swipe, release, then navigate**.

## Expected interaction

- The destination/source view should track horizontal drag progress continuously where the navigation pattern supports it.
- Reversing the gesture before the commit threshold should naturally cancel and return to the origin.
- Crossing the commit threshold should complete from the current interactive position rather than starting a second delayed animation.
- Gesture velocity/distance should produce predictable completion behavior.
- A partial gesture must not accidentally change selected item/session state before the transition commits.

## Investigation

Determine whether the current implementation uses a discrete swipe recognizer or state change followed by a separate navigation animation rather than an interactive transition.

Also verify that attempts to make the transition interactive do not expose the broader performance regression tracked in #93. The transition should remain directly coupled to touch under realistic loaded-library conditions.

## Accessibility / platform behavior

- Preserve ordinary button/navigation alternatives; swipe must not become the only route.
- Respect Reduce Motion with an appropriate system-consistent transition while preserving prompt input response.
- VoiceOver focus must end on the correct destination after commit and remain on the origin after cancellation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] During a supported horizontal navigation swipe, visible transition progress tracks finger movement rather than waiting until gesture completion.
- [ ] Reversing/cancelling a partial swipe returns smoothly to the original screen without changing the selected target.
- [ ] Committing the swipe completes from the current gesture progress without a perceptible pause/restart.
- [ ] Slow drags, fast flicks, aborted gestures, repeated swipes, and edge-of-screen interactions behave deterministically.
- [ ] Interaction remains responsive on a physical device with a realistic loaded library.
- [ ] VoiceOver and Reduce Motion behavior remains correct.
